issue_context.title: Process Exits on Invalid PRAGMA with DuckDB Golang Binding
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

I'm experiencing an issue with the DuckDB Golang binding (go-duckdb v1.5.6) where executing a PRAGMA statement with a non-existent function causes the process to exit unexpectedly. 

### To Reproduce

```go
package main

import (
	"database/sql"
	_ "github.com/marcboeker/go-duckdb"
)

func main() {
	db, _ := sql.Open("duckdb", "")
	_, _ = db.Query(`PRAGMA something`)
}

```

Outputs:
```
libc++abi.dylib: terminating with uncaught exception of type duckdb::CatalogException: Catalog Error: Pragma Function with name something does not exist!
Did you mean "show"?
SIGABRT: abort
PC=0x7fff20423462 m=0 sigcode=0
signal arrived during cgo execution

```

### OS:

MacOS 11.2.3

### DuckDB Version:

v0.9.2(source_id: 3c695d7)

### DuckDB Client:

go-duckdb v1.5.6

### Full Name:

Yang Ou

### Affiliation:

Duozhuayu

### Have you tried this on the latest `main` branch?

I have tested with a release build (and could not test with a main build)

### Have you tried the steps to reproduce? Do they include all relevant data and configuration? Does the issue you report still appear there?

- [X] Yes, I have
comments: Thanks, I could reproduce the issue. The problem seems to occur within the Go binding, so I opened an issue there (with the content of this issue): https://github.com/marcboeker/go-duckdb/issues/142
Thanks @marcboeker for clarifying this. We'll look into it.

review_comments:
There's a reason we catch both `duckdb::Exception` and `std::exception` here - `PreservedError` looks at the exception type from `duckdb::Exception` and uses that to print the error type prefix (e.g. `Catalog Error: ...`).

I'm actually removing all of this in my exception refactor - but currently removing this branch changes behavior
I suppose this is the actual fix? My rework is fixing this as well since we're moving all of the catches to `std::exception` everywhere. I'll add the test case to my rework.

Yes, this is the fix.
> I'll add the test case to my rework.

Perfect! So we'll only catch `std::exception` in the C API from now on?

Also, should I then close this PR? What are the plans for the `FIXME`s, i.e., cases where we only return `DuckDBError` to the user, and omit the actual exception message?

Yes, we'll only need to catch `std::exception` after my rework (in the C API and elsewhere).

Let's close this PR to avoid merge conflicts - if required you can add the FIXME's later. The problem is that we can't always easily return the actual error message (and often it is not interesting either, e.g. a lot of the catches are there just to catch memory allocation failures so they basically never happen in practice).

As a note - these `catch(...)` branches are more safeguards against programmer error - they should not happen unless someone throws an exception that does not derive from `std::exception` (e.g. `throw "Error"`).

Gotcha. I was wondering about this, also because of the other exception types [here](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/try_catch).
```cpp
try
{
    f();
}
catch (const [std::overflow_error](http://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/error/overflow_error)& e)
{} // this executes if f() throws std::overflow_error (same type rule)
catch (const [std::runtime_error](http://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/error/runtime_error)& e)
{} // this executes if f() throws std::underflow_error (base class rule)
catch (const [std::exception](http://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/error/exception)& e)
{} // this executes if f() throws std::logic_error (base class rule)
catch (...)
{} // this executes if f() throws std::string or int or any other unrelated type
```
